tokyo_paichi.price_note: ⚠ PRICES MAY NOT INCLUDE TAX. Tabelog carries an explicit warning on this listing — 「税込金額か不明の価格です。正確な価格は店舗へ直接ご確認ください」, meaning it does not know whether these figures are tax-inclusive and says to confirm with the shop. Every other record in this dataset states tax-included prices, so this one is the exception and the numbers below could be up to 10% higher at the till. ⚠ ON THE FOOD: 洋食 is Japan's domesticated Western cooking, and it is one of the most consistently wheat-heavy categories there is — the fried section is flour, egg and panko throughout, the stews are built on a browned roux, and the curry is a roux curry. There is no gluten-free order on this menu and the salads are the only things that come close. A vegan has less than that: even the plain 生野菜 salad is the only item with no declared animal ingredient, and its dressing is unstated. Recorded in full so the answer is visible rather than absent. 浅草1-15-1; closed Sundays; lunch 11:30–14:00 and dinner 17:00–20:00. Note the shop's own remark that from two portions the stew arrives in one shared pot.

tokyo_nikujiru_suigyoza_gyopao.price_note: Prices tax-included as printed by the shop. ⚠ THIS SHOP LABELS ITS OWN VEGETARIAN DISHES — six items carry a 【ベジタリアン】 mark, which is rare in Tokyo and genuinely useful. But read the word carefully: ベジタリアン means VEGETARIAN, not vegan. The gelato and the soy pudding both carry the mark, and one of those is far more likely to suit a vegan than the other. The label also says nothing about gluten, and this is a DUMPLING shop — the house speciality is water gyoza, and every wrapper, bun and roll on the board is wheat. The clean split here is that the labelled vegetable dishes are also the only dishes with any gluten prospect, because they are the ones with no wrapper. No allergen statement beyond the vegetarian marks. The signature 肉汁水餃子 is ¥1,089 for four, ¥1,420 for six and ¥2,380 for ten, made with 100% Kagoshima black pork.

tokyo_shinjuku_kominka_juttoku.price_note: No menu published anywhere readable. The shop's own site carries its concept, hours and seating but no dishes and no prices; the Tabelog menu page returns 404. The five dishes below are ones visitors name having eaten, with NO PRICES because no visitor states one — Tabelog gives only a ¥5,000–5,999 band for the shop. ⚠ WHAT THIS KIND OF PLACE MEANS FOR BOTH DIETS: it bills itself as 全国郷土の味巡り, a tour of regional Japanese cooking, in a converted old house — and regional washoku is the category where DASHI and SOY SAUCE are in nearly everything, including dishes that look plain. Bonito dashi is a vegan fact and a gluten fact at once, since 白だし, めんつゆ and だし醤油 are all soy-based. A sake izakaya is also a barley room: beer is barley and 麦焼酎 is barley, neither flagged by Japanese allergen labelling. One thing a visitor establishes that is genuinely useful: at lunch, rice and miso soup come with free refills. Open from 16:00 Tuesday to Friday; 50 seats with tatami and counter. Note for the record: a visitor mentions 十徳新宿本店 was closed for renovation to the end of August and trading from an annexe — that is the separate HONTEN, not this shop, and is not recorded as a closure here.

tokyo_waiwaitei.price_note: ⚠ TWO PRICE WARNINGS, BOTH FROM TABELOG ITSELF. First, this menu carries an update date of 2019/06/24 — it is about seven years old, so treat every figure as historical. Second, Tabelog states 「税込金額か不明の価格です。正確な価格は店舗へ直接ご確認ください」: it does not know whether these prices include tax. Most records in this dataset state tax-inclusive prices; this is the second one that cannot. ⚠ THE ONE THING ON THIS MENU WORTH A COELIAC'S ATTENTION, and it needs stating carefully because it is not confirmed: the pizza section contains a line reading 野菜ライス生地PIZZA — a vegetable RICE-DOUGH pizza. A rice-flour base at an Italian restaurant would be a genuine find. But the listing is ambiguous about whether that line is a dish or a heading introducing a rice-dough crust option for the pizzas beneath it, it carries no price, and NO GLUTEN-FREE CLAIM IS MADE ANYWHERE. Even if the base is rice, it would be rolled on the same bench and baked in the same oven as wheat dough. Worth a phone call; not worth an assumption. A second alternative crust, じゃことたまご生地PIZZA (whitebait and egg dough, ¥800), sits nearby and is equally undescribed. Otherwise this is a pasta-and-pizza house and the answer is uniform. Two accommodation notes the shop does volunteer: 「辛さ調整いたします」 (heat adjusted to taste) and 「ご要望ございましたらその他お作りいたします」 (they will make other things on request) — which is the sort of kitchen where asking is worth doing. tokyo_hokkaido_meibutsu_ramen_.price_note: Prices tax-included as printed by the shop. No allergen statement. ⚠ Two straightforward facts and one worth pausing on. The straightforward ones: this is a ramen shop, ramen noodles are WHEAT, and every broth here is a 甘エビ (sweet shrimp) stock, so nothing on the board suits a vegan and nothing suits a coeliac. The one worth pausing on is the NOODLE CHOICE — the shop invites you to pick 太麺 or 細麺, thick or thin. That is the situation where someone might hope a shop offers a rice or buckwheat alternative, and here as at other shops in this dataset the choice is between two kinds of wheat. Recorded in full so the answer is visible rather than absent. No reservations; 西新宿7-8-2, three minutes from Shinjuku-nishiguchi.
